attrs.rationale: Both fields perform the same core activities: verifying conservative extension properties, validating subsumptions, and checking concept inseparability. They work jointly on reasoning correctness.
Formal methods verification provides the theoretical framework and techniques that knowledge base validation applies to verify conservative extension properties and validate ontology extensions.
Knowledge base validation checks and audits the output of knowledge representation systems development to ensure conservative extension properties and correct subsumption validation.
Knowledge representation systems development requires logical reasoning system implementation to provide the reasoning capabilities needed to verify conservative extensions and validate subsumptions.
Logical reasoning system implementation provides the reasoning infrastructure that ontology consistency checking uses to verify logical consistency and conservative extension properties.
Ontology consistency checking validates the output of ontology engineering by verifying conservative extension properties and ensuring no new subsumptions are entailed.
Ontology engineering depends on ontology maintenance and versioning to manage the lifecycle of ontologies and ensure conservative extension properties across versions.
Ontology maintenance and versioning provides the ontology artifacts and version management that ontology module extraction uses to extract modules with logical guarantees.
Ontology module extraction provides extracted modules with logical guarantees that query answering system design uses to perform ontology-mediated query answering correctly.
Query answering system design depends on description logic reasoning to verify conservative extension properties and perform concept inseparability checking for correct query answers.
